title: Support Worker
description:
About this role

Search Consultancy are currently recruiting for Support Workers to join our ever expanding Bank Hours team within the Bradford area. We are currently operating a fast track recruitment process with next day interviews available and free DBS checks.

We are recruiting Support Workers on a temporary / ad hoc basis to work in various private healthcare settings, supporting service users with mental health illnesses and learning difficulties.

Key Responsibilities

Support individuals with daily living tasks
Assist with mobility and safe moving & handling
Support with meals and hydration
Promote independence and encourage choice
Monitor wellbeing and report concerns appropriately
Maintain accurate records and follow care plans
The suitable candidates will:

Have worked a minimum of 6 months recent experience in a healthcare setting.
Have a flexible approach towards work.
Be able to travel via own or public transport in local and surrounding areas to your home.
What we offer:

Free DBS check (Limited time only)
Free specialist training programmes.
100% Flexible working hours to fit around any lifestyle.
Experience in a variety of high quality Support and Care environments.
Competitive rates of pay.
You will need to have a minimum of six months' recent UK experience working within a healthcare environment in a similar capacity. Shortlisted applicants will be required to attend a video interview.

All positions are subject to an enhanced DBS check and we require a minimum of two satisfactory employment references. Although shifts are offered on an ad hoc basis, work is constantly ongoing.

(AGY) Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

Whether you're looking to top up your income, fit work around family commitments, or choose when and where you work, we offer flexible agency shifts across a range of high-quality healthcare services.

We're recruiting now with a fast-track recruitment process, next-day video interviews, and a free enhanced DBS for successful applicants (limited-time offer).

The Role
You'll support adults in specialist healthcare settings, working with individuals with mental health needs and learning disabilities. Every shift offers the opportunity to make a genuine difference while gaining experience across a variety of services.

Responsibilities
Supporting individuals with day-to-day living activities
Promoting independence, dignity and choice
Assisting with mobility and safe moving & handling
Supporting with meals, hydration and personal wellbeing
Observing and reporting changes in service users' wellbeing
Completing accurate records and following individual care plans

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Learning Care Assistant
description:
Job Title: Learning Care Assistant
Location: Wakefield
Start Date: ASAP
Salary: £95 - £110 per day

Do you have experience supporting children and young people with Profound and Multiple Learning Difficulties (PMLD) and complex needs?

Are you passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of children and young people with additional needs?

Do you have a caring, patient and adaptable approach to supporting students with their learning and personal development?

TeacherActive is proud to be working with a specialist SEND school based in Wakefield, supporting children and young people aged 2 to 19 with Profound and Multiple Learning Difficulties (PMLD) and complex needs. The setting is dedicated to providing a supportive and inclusive learning environment where students can develop their independence, communication and personal skills.

The school is looking to appoint a dedicated Learning Care Assistant on a full-time, long-term basis, starting ASAP. The successful Learning Care Assistant will support students with a range of complex learning and physical needs, providing individualised support with learning activities, personal care and daily routines while working closely with teaching staff to ensure each student's needs are met.

The successful Learning Care Assistant will have:
- Relevant qualifications in Health and Social Care, Supporting Teaching and Learning or a related field (desirable)
- Experience supporting children or young people with PMLD and complex needs
- Previous experience working in a children's care setting (desirable)
- Confidence supporting students with personal care, communication and individual learning needs
- A patient, caring and nurturing approach to supporting vulnerable children and young people
- Excellent communication skills, adaptability and a positive 'can-do' attitude

In return for the above you can expect to receive:
- A dedicated team of consultants available 24/7 to help you with the easy onboarding process
- CPD courses and certificates as part of the My-Progression channel
- Market leading rates of pay
- TeacherActive Referral Scheme - Receive up to £100 when you refer a friend Terms and Conditions apply

Our staff are paid on a PAYE basis, so you can rest assured that you re paying the right level of TAX and National Insurance and there s no messing around with admin charges coming out of your hard earned cash.

If you are an enthusiastic Learning Care Assistant looking for a rewarding opportunity within a specialist SEND setting, then click APPLY NOW and I will be in touch regarding this fantastic opportunity.

title: Complex Care Support Worker
description:
Complex Support Worker - Female only:

This post is exempt under the Equality Act 2010 as there is a genuine occupational need to recruit Females due to the nature of the role.

Dedicated day shifts (with flexibility for occasional sleepovers if required). Full-time and part-time positions available.

We are looking to recruit 4 Specialist Support Workers to join an already established, experienced, and highly supportive care team. You will be working together to provide consistent, high-quality care for a young lady, who lives in her own home alongside her parents.

Joining an existing team means you will have plenty of support, and a well-structured routine to step into, and the opportunity to learn from colleagues who already know daily routines and preferences inside out.

Key Clinical & Behavioral Responsibilities:
- Epilepsy Management & Rescue Medication: Monitoring and managing complex epilepsy, including absence, clonic, and tonic seizures. Administering emergency rescue medication (Buccal Midazolam) when required.
- Positive Behaviour Support: To understand behavior as communication, defuse anxiety-based behaviors, and maintain a calm, structured, and capable environment.
- Communication & Interaction: supporting with communication support tailored to Autism (ASD) to help her express choices and reduce frustration.
- Daily Living: Providing respectful personal care and full continence management.

Shift Patterns:
- Primarily day shifts.
- Flexibility is required to cover a shared team rota, with an occasional requirement for sleepover shifts and respite.

Duties also include working towards person centred care plans, using a low demand approach, de-escalation techniques and role play, assisting with daily activities and outings/appointments, in addition ensuring excellent documentation and record keeping is maintained, there may be requirement for personal care including continence care.

Successful candidates will have previous UK paid experience of at least Six month's within the last 2 years within a similar healthcare setting.

What We Are Looking For:
- Prior experience or formal training in administering Buccal Midazolam is highly preferred
- Experience working with individuals on the Autism Spectrum (ASD) who display behaviors that challenge, ideally using PBS (Positive Behaviour Support) principles.
- A resilient, observant, and team-focused nature.
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively alongside the family and existing care team.

Applications are reviewed as they are received, we do not provide feedback for unsuccessful applications. We can only accept applications from candidates who are located in and eligible to work within the UK - This post is not open to Sponsorship under the UKVI scheme, and we are unable to accept applicants with Skilled Worker Visas.

Precedo Healthcare is a passionate, inclusive, and anti-racist organisation. We actively encourage applications from candidates from all backgrounds and cultures, however we can only accept fully completed applications from those located in and eligible to work within the UK.

If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or in the workplace due to a disability, please inform us promptly. We are committed to providing appropriate support throughout your journey with us.

Precedo Healthcare is member of JobsAware.

To stay safe in your job search we recommend that you visit JobSAware, a non-profit, joint industry and law enforcement organisation working to combat job scams. Visit the JobsAware website for information on common scams and to get free, expert advice for a safer job search.
